subject: Urgent: Emberlane p95 latency & error surge after v4.1 quant rollout
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@emberlane.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@emberlane.com>, PlatformOps <ops@emberlane.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:14:00Z
Subject: Sudden p95 jump + 504s after your v4.1 deploy

Connor —

We're seeing a dramatic regression in tail latency and a rising 5xx rate after the model update you pushed to our production route this morning (v4.1, q4-per-tensor profile). p95 went from ~220ms to ~1.2s and our API is returning intermittent 504s. This started around 08:30 PST after the automatic rollout.

Attached are a short sample of request IDs (emberlane_request_ids.txt) and a 2MB collection of logs (emberlane_error_samples.log). Example request IDs: req_20261122_08:33:15_az7f, req_20261122_08:39:47_b6q9. Errors correlate with higher time_in_queue and occasional "kv-cache-miss->cpu-fallback" traces in the logs.

We flagged this as Sev2. We need an immediate mitigation: either rollback to the previous model variant (v4.0-q8) for our traffic or a hotfix we can configure on our side. Also, please escalate to an exec contact — our CTO is on standby.

Thanks,
Sara
Director of AI Ops, Emberlane

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Holt <sara.holt@emberlane.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump + 504s after your v4.1 deploy — initial triage

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Timeline: v4.1 rolled globally at ~08:28 PST with new q4 per-tensor profile (smaller activations but different dequant path).
- Symptoms seen: p95 increase, queueing at the request router, intermittent 504s when downstream runtime workers hit CPU fallback for KV cache operations.
- Root cause hypothesis: On Emberlane's fleet (A100s w/ driver 470.x), the new per-tensor q4 kernels trigger a code path that performs dequantization on CPU for certain sequence-length distributions and KV cache sizes; this increases token latency and produces contention on the host. We also see an uptick in memcpy throughput on PCIe vs NVLINK in the traces you sent.
- Notable: The v4.1 build also included a small tokenizer normalization change (whitespace handling) that increases average tokenization time for a subset of inputs — this amplifies the per-request cost at high QPS.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now (in-flight):
1) Rolling Emberlane back to v4.0-q8 (Connor/Marissa doing that).
2) If rollback not feasible for any reason, we can pin Emberlane's route to v4.1 but force the runtime to use the legacy q8 dequant path (hotfix flag: runtime.force_q8_dequant=true) — this avoids the CPU dequant fallback at the cost of ~8% token accuracy loss.
3) Short-term runtime knobs: lower per-worker concurrency for Emberlane routes (concurrency=8), increase worker count for the account, and disable continuous-batching for their routes to reduce head-of-line latency.

Next steps for postmortem: collect kernel traces, PCIe metrics, and a tokenization perf diff between v4.0 and v4.1 on Emberlane's sample corpus. I'll attach a diff (v4.0-to-v4.1-quant-diff.patch) to the incident.

—Naomi
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Exec update: Emberlane stabilization and next steps

Sara/Tom — quick executive note following our stabilization yesterday:
- Immediate mitigation: traffic rolled back to v4.0-q8 and p95 stabilized.
- Root-cause hypothesis: v4.1 per-tensor q4 kernel triggered CPU dequant fallback on Emberlane's specific GPU/driver configuration, compounded by a tokenizer perf delta.
- Short-term: we will not reintroduce v4.1 to Emberlane until Q1 2027 work is complete (kernel patches + extended perf tests).
- Compensation: pending formal review, but Marissa has opened a 10% service credit for the impacted window and will route the request to billing.
- Next exec touchpoint: we propose a 30-minute call this week with Emberlane CTO and our Head of Infrastructure to review timeline and any contractual concerns.

Attaching the postmortem draft to the incident and scheduling the technical review. Thanks again for the patience and the detailed logs — they made root cause repro much faster.

—Connor
